records.note: Ironic aside ('not in jail. At least, not yet') in a satire-framed post about Haemanthus. The words insinuate that Billy Evans may be jailed but name no charge, case, court or date. Read sincerely there is still no event to write without inventing a case.

'This will go big or go home' covers every outcome, so no event, benchmark or threshold can be written for Haemanthus. 'Get out your checkbooks, investors' is sarcasm; the sincere reading (the device is physically implausible) is a judgment, not an observable event.

Characterization of Haemanthus as 'implausible testing that raises millions'. Descriptive, present tense; no future state is asserted in the words. The implied failure of the technology has no event, source or date.
Announcement of the forecaster's own RAMHT LA 2025 event (he is the organizer). Own-organization event; not scored.

States a regulatory requirement as information: more data are needed before PRISM (GrayMatters Health) gets FDA clearance for depression. Eventual clearance is presupposed, not asserted, and no lexicon phrase is present. The same post says a depression clearance was 'just' obtained, so the target decision is unclear. Not coded as a forecast.
Promise of the forecaster's own newsletter content ('I will dig into more soon'). Own publication; not scored.
'May prove another practical option for treating depression' names no deciding body, benchmark, threshold, series or date for PRISM. No event can be written.
Slogan: 'The future of mental health is effective'. No entity, event, benchmark or date.
Statement of the forecaster's stance on his own litigation ('leaving to the courts to settle'). No ruling direction or future state is asserted; the dispute is also outside the five areas.

Police use of lethal force in mental-health crisis calls, from a 2020 recording republished in 2025. Not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice-adoption outcome. Also a generalized behavioural claim with no dated event.
Police killings of Black Americans, from the same 2020 recording. Outside the five areas; generalized claim with no dated event.
Own-newsletter schedule ('fresh new content' after the forecaster finishes editing a trial publication). Own publication; not scored.

'Which jobs AI will displace' presupposes displacement of some jobs with no countable set, series, threshold or date. The main clause ('I have initiated the trend by displacing myself') is retrospective.

'Is something we can feel good about automating away' is an evaluation of automating TD screening, not an asserted future state. No scale, series or date. TDscreen.ai is a Videra Health product, where the forecaster is a strategic advisor.
'Provides hope that more and more screening tasks can be accomplished' is a hedged quantifier ('more and more') with no countable set, benchmark or date.
Radial (the forecaster is Chief Medical Officer) expanding to more states ('we are working on it'). Own-company expansion; not scored.
Vulnerable insomnia patients 'will be treated with' zolpidem: a general practice claim with no countable set, series, threshold or date.
Implicit promise of a future article in the forecaster's own newsletter. Own publication; not scored.
General claim that venture-funded founders will not reject the pharma business model. No named company, countable set, benchmark or date.
'You're never going to get a company funded with that attitude' is a general, hyperbolic claim with no named company, funding round, countable set or date.
Clinical opinion that ketamine is 'unlikely to be helpful as a first-line treatment' in severe personality disorders. No trial, endpoint, deciding body, series or date; no event can be written.

'Before their world ends, from a stock price standpoint' asserts a UnitedHealth Group stock decline with no threshold, series or date: a comparative without a benchmark. The sentence also opens a satirical fake press release, so the framing is hyperbolic.
Radial (the forecaster's company) adding locations 'soon'. Own-company expansion; not scored. 'Soon' is also not a deadline.

The forecaster is a co-author ('middle author') on the 'forthcoming' BrainsWay accelerated Deep TMS paper. Publication of the forecaster's own paper is a CONTROL item under the prompt's list; the sentence is also a statement of authorship, not an expectation.
Radial (the forecaster's company) 'more soon' on locations, restating owen-1770 in a later post. Own-company expansion; not scored.
Own-newsletter schedule: a podcast episode 'tomorrow'. Own publication; not scored.
Promise of the forecaster's own future writing about his father. Own publication; not scored.
The forecaster's own next task (editing a podcast episode). Own activity; not scored.

'The replication will be challenging' has no benchmark, trial, threshold or date for the MOAM (MBT-ASPD) result; 'a moral imperative' is normative. The second sentence ('This is a revolution, assuming it replicates, and if only decision makers notice') is a slogan under a double condition with no event. The forecaster is an MBT supervisor, but the item fails before affiliation matters.

The sentence is already captured in full inside the quote of owen-1776 (same post); the first row stands. On its own it would fail as VAGUE: 'revolution' is a slogan, and the double condition (replication, decision-maker attention) names no observable event, source or date.

'Even more excellent data on TMS is coming' has no countable set (which trials), no benchmark for 'excellent' and no date ('is coming' is not a deadline). The forecaster is a BrainsWay trial investigator, but the item fails before affiliation matters.

'I look forward to reading the paper' is a statement of anticipation about the COMP360 trial publication, not an asserted future state. The trial result itself (primary endpoint met) was already public on the statement date.

The forecaster's skeptical restatement of the HHS/CMS prior-authorization announcement ('a new day is almost here, sorta'). 'A new day' is a slogan; no observable event, benchmark or date can be written from the words.

'We will see if health plans can hold it together or will resort to other solutions' states no direction in words, and 'hold it together' has no benchmark, series or date for the insurer prior-authorization pledges. The purity-pledge analogy is tone, which is not read.

'This probably works pretty well for them' concerns Tutanota LLC's profit from a mini-tender for UnitedHealth Group shares at $325. Tutanota's profit is not publicly observable, the offer expiration date is not in the text, and 'works' is not tied to a single observable criterion in the words. No event can be written without inventing the resolution.

'And it probably works!' restates owen-1785 in the same post about the Tutanota mini-tender. Present-tense description of the strategy; no public series, threshold, expiration date or observable criterion in the words.
'Could heal deep regions of the brain ... could do a lot of things' is a capability claim for tFUS with no trial, endpoint, regulator, series or date.
'Might heal depression' for tFUS (Sanmai) names no trial, endpoint, regulator, threshold or date; the cited RCT graphic is not in the text.
'Might heal anxiety' for tFUS names no trial, endpoint, regulator, threshold or date.
'Might heal PTSD ... and dozens of other brain disorders' names no trial, endpoint, regulator, threshold or date; 'dozens' has no countable set.
